L22: 【8†Lemma 30.16.1.】 Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $X \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(R)$ be a proper morphism. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample invertible sheaf on $X$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module.
L23: 
L24:   1. The graded ring $A = \bigoplus _{d \geq 0} H^0(X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d})$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra.
L25: 
L26:   2. There exists an $r \geq 0$ and $d_1, \ldots , d_ r \in \mathbf{Z}$ and a surjection
L27: \[ \bigoplus \nolimits _{j = 1, \ldots , r} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d_ j} \longrightarrow \mathcal{F}. \]
L28: 
L29:   3. For any $p$ the cohomology group $H^ p(X, \mathcal{F})$ is a finite $R$-module.
L30: 
L31:   4. If $p > 0$, then $H^ p(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes _{\mathcal{O}_ X} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}) = 0$ for all $d$ large enough.
L32: 
L33:   5. For any $k \in \mathbf{Z}$ the graded $A$-module
L34: 
L35: \[ \bigoplus \nolimits _{d \geq k} H^0(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes _{\mathcal{O}_ X} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}) \]
L36: 
L37: is a finite $A$-module.
L38: Proof. By Morphisms, Lemma 【14†29.40.4】 there exists a $d > 0$ and an immersion $i : X \to \mathbf{P}^ n_ R$ such that $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes d} \cong i^*\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^ n_ R}(1)$. Since $X$ is proper over $R$ the morphism $i$ is a closed immersion (Morphisms, Lemma 【15†29.42.7】).
L39: Thus we have $H^ i(X, \mathcal{G}) = H^ i(\mathbf{P}^ n_ R, i_*\mathcal{G})$ for any quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ on $X$ (by Lemma 【16†30.2.4】 and the fact that closed immersions are affine, see Morphisms, Lemma 【17†29.11.10】). Moreover, if $\mathcal{G}$ is coherent, then $i_*\mathcal{G}$ is coherent as well (Lemma 【18†30.9.8】). We will use these facts without further mention.
L40: Proof of (1). Set $S = R[T_0, \ldots , T_ n]$ so that $\mathbf{P}^ n_ R = \text{Proj}(S)$. Observe that $A$ is an $S$-algebra (but the ring map $S \to A$ is not a homomorphism of graded rings because $S_ n$ maps into $A_{dn}$). By the projection formula (Cohomology, Lemma 【19†20.54.2】) we have
L41: 
L42: \[ i_*(\mathcal{L}^{\otimes nd + q}) = i_*(\mathcal{L}^{\otimes q}) \otimes _{\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^ n_ R}} \mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^ n_ R}(n) \]
L43: for all $n \in \mathbf{Z}$. We conclude that $\bigoplus _{n \geq 0} A_{nd + q}$ is a finite graded $S$-module by Lemma 【20†30.14.1】. Since $A = \bigoplus _{q \in \{ 0, \ldots , d - 1} \bigoplus _{n \geq 0} A_{nd + q}$ we see that $A$ is finite as an $S$-algebra, hence (1) is true.
L44: 
L45: Proof of (2). This follows from Properties, Proposition 【21†28.27.13】.
L46: 
L47: Proof of (3). Apply Lemma 【20†30.14.1】 and use $H^ p(X, \mathcal{F}) = H^ p(\mathbf{P}^ n_ R, i_*\mathcal{F})$.
L48: Proof of (4). Fix $p > 0$. By the projection formula we have
L49: 
L50: \[ i_*(\mathcal{F} \otimes _{\mathcal{O}_ X} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes nd + q}) = i_*(\mathcal{F} \otimes _{\mathcal{O}_ X} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes q}) \otimes _{\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^ n_ R}} \mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^ n_ R}(n) \]
L51: for all $n \in \mathbf{Z}$. By Lemma 【20†30.14.1】 we conclude that $H^ p(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{nd + q}) = 0$ for $n \gg 0$. Since there are only finitely many congruence classes of integers modulo $d$ this proves (4).
L52: Proof of (5). Fix an integer $k$. Set $M = \bigoplus _{n \geq k} H^0(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$. Arguing as above we conclude that $\bigoplus _{nd + q \geq k} M_{nd + q}$ is a finite graded $S$-module. Since $M = \bigoplus _{q \in \{ 0, \ldots , d - 1\} } \bigoplus _{nd + q \geq k} M_{nd + q}$ we see that $M$ is finite as an $S$-module. Since the $S$-module structure factors through the ring map $S \to A$, we conclude that $M$ is finite as an $A$-module. $\square$

L22: 【8†Lemma 33.45.1.】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module. Let $\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots , \mathcal{L}_ r$ be invertible $\mathcal{O}_ X$-modules. The map
L23: 
L24: \[ (n_1, \ldots , n_ r) \longmapsto \chi (X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes \mathcal{L}_ r^{\otimes n_ r}) \]
L25: 
L26: is a numerical polynomial in $n_1, \ldots , n_ r$ of total degree at most the dimension of the support of $\mathcal{F}$.
L27: Proof. We prove this by induction on $\dim (\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}))$. If this number is zero, then the function is constant with value $\dim _ k \Gamma (X, \mathcal{F})$ by Lemma 【14†33.33.3】. Assume $\dim (\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})) > 0$.
L28: If $\mathcal{F}$ has embedded associated points, then we can consider the short exact sequence $0 \to \mathcal{K} \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}' \to 0$ constructed in Divisors, Lemma 【15†31.4.6】. Since the dimension of the support of $\mathcal{K}$ is strictly less, the result holds for $\mathcal{K}$ by induction hypothesis and with strictly smaller total degree. By additivity of the Euler characteristic (Lemma 【16†33.33.2】) it suffices to prove the result for $\mathcal{F}'$.
L29: Thus we may assume $\mathcal{F}$ does not have embedded associated points.
L30: If $i : Z \to X$ is a closed immersion and $\mathcal{F} = i_*\mathcal{G}$, then we see that the result for $X$, $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots , \mathcal{L}_ r$ is equivalent to the result for $Z$, $\mathcal{G}$, $i^*\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots , i^*\mathcal{L}_ r$ (since the cohomologies agree, see Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 【17†30.2.4】). Applying Divisors, Lemma 【18†31.4.7】 we may assume that $X$ has no embedded components and $X = \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$.
L31: Pick a regular meromorphic section $s$ of $\mathcal{L}_1$, see Divisors, Lemma 【19†31.26.4】. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_ X$ be the ideal of denominators of $s$ and consider the maps
L32: 
L33: \[ \mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F},\quad \mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}_1 \]
L34: of Divisors, Lemma 【20†31.25.5】. These are injective and have cokernels $\mathcal{Q}$, $\mathcal{Q}'$ supported on nowhere dense closed subschemes of $X = \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$. Tensoring with the invertible module $\mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes \mathcal{L}_ r^{\otimes n_ r}$ is exact, hence using additivity again we see that
L35: \begin{align*} & \chi (X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes \mathcal{L}_ r^{\otimes n_ r}) - \chi (X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1 + 1} \otimes \ldots \otimes \mathcal{L}_ r^{\otimes n_ r}) \\ & = \chi (\mathcal{Q} \otimes \mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes \mathcal{L}_ r^{\otimes n_ r}) - \chi (\mathcal{Q}' \otimes \mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes \mathcal{L}_ r^{\otimes n_ r}) \end{align*}
L36: Thus we see that the function $P(n_1, \ldots , n_ r)$ of the lemma has the property that
L37: 
L38: \[ P(n_1 + 1, n_2, \ldots , n_ r) - P(n_1, \ldots , n_ r) \]
L39: 
L40: is a numerical polynomial of total degree $<$ the dimension of the support of $\mathcal{F}$. Of course by symmetry the same thing is true for
L41: 
L42: \[ P(n_1, \ldots , n_{i - 1}, n_ i + 1, n_{i + 1}, \ldots , n_ r) - P(n_1, \ldots , n_ r) \]
L43: for any $i \in \{ 1, \ldots , r\} $. A simple arithmetic argument shows that $P$ is a numerical polynomial of total degree at most $\dim (\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}))$. $\square$

L23: 【8†Proposition 28.27.13.】 Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $X$. Set $S = \Gamma _*(X, \mathcal{L})$. The following are equivalent:
L24: 
L25:   1. $\mathcal{L}$ is ample,
L26: 
L27:   2. the open sets $X_ s$, with $s \in S_{+}$ homogeneous, cover $X$ and the associated morphism $X \to \text{Proj}(S)$ is an open immersion,
L28: 
L29:   3. the open sets $X_ s$, with $s \in S_{+}$ homogeneous, form a basis for the topology of $X$,
L30:   4. the open sets $X_ s$, with $s \in S_{+}$ homogeneous, which are affine form a basis for the topology of $X$,
L31: 
L32:   5. for every quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ the sum of the images of the canonical maps
L33: 
L34: \[ \Gamma (X, \mathcal{F} \otimes _{\mathcal{O}_ X} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}) \otimes _{\mathbf{Z}} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes -n} \longrightarrow \mathcal{F} \]
L35: 
L36: with $n \geq 1$ equals $\mathcal{F}$,
L37:   6. same property as (【15†5】) with $\mathcal{F}$ ranging over all quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals,
L38: 
L39:   7. $X$ is quasi-separated and for every quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ of finite type on $X$ there exists an integer $n_0$ such that $\mathcal{F} \otimes _{\mathcal{O}_ X} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}$ is globally generated for all $n \geq n_0$,
L40:   8. $X$ is quasi-separated and for every quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ of finite type on $X$ there exist integers $n > 0$, $k \geq 0$ such that $\mathcal{F}$ is a quotient of a direct sum of $k$ copies of $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes - n}$, and
L41: 
L42:   9. same as in (【16†8】) with $\mathcal{F}$ ranging over all sheaves of ideals of finite type on $X$.
L43: Proof. Lemma 【17†28.27.11】 is (【18†1】) $\Rightarrow $ (【19†2】). Lemmas 【20†28.27.2】 and 【10†28.27.12】 provide the implication (【18†1】) $\Leftarrow $ (【19†2】). The implications (【19†2】) $\Rightarrow $ (【21†4】) $\Rightarrow $ (【22†3】) are clear from Constructions, Section 【23†27.8】. Lemma 【24†28.27.6】 is (【22†3】) $\Rightarrow $ (【18†1】). Thus we see that the first 4 conditions are all equivalent.
L44: Assume the equivalent conditions (1) – (4). Note that in particular $X$ is separated (as an open subscheme of the separated scheme $\text{Proj}(S)$). Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$. Choose $s \in S_{+}$ homogeneous such that $X_ s$ is affine. We claim that any section $m \in \Gamma (X_ s, \mathcal{F})$ is in the image of one of the maps displayed in (【15†5】) above. This will imply (【15†5】) since these affines $X_ s$ cover $X$.
L45: Namely, by Lemma 【25†28.18.2】 we may write $m$ as the image of $m' \otimes s^{-n}$ for some $n \geq 1$, some $m' \in \Gamma (X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$. This proves the claim.
L46: Clearly (【15†5】) $\Rightarrow $ (【26†6】). Let us assume (【26†6】) and prove $\mathcal{L}$ is ample. Pick $x \in X$. Let $U \subset X$ be an affine open which contains $x$. Set $Z = X \setminus U$. We may think of $Z$ as a reduced closed subscheme, see Schemes, Section 【27†26.12】. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_ X$ be the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals corresponding to the closed subscheme $Z$.
L47: By assumption (【26†6】), there exists an $n \geq 1$ and a section $s \in \Gamma (X, \mathcal{I} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$ such that $s$ does not vanish at $x$ (more precisely such that $s \not\in \mathfrak m_ x \mathcal{I}_ x \otimes \mathcal{L}_ x^{\otimes n}$). We may think of $s$ as a section of $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}$. Since it clearly vanishes along $Z$ we see that $X_ s \subset U$. Hence $X_ s$ is affine, see Lemma 【28†28.27.4】. This proves that $\mathcal{L}$ is ample.
L48: At this point we have proved that (1) – (6) are equivalent.
L49: Assume the equivalent conditions (1) – (6). In the following we will use the fact that the tensor product of two sheaves of modules which are globally generated is globally generated without further mention (see Modules, Lemma 【29†17.4.3】). By (1) we can find elements $s_ i \in S_{d_ i}$ with $d_ i \geq 1$ such that $X = \bigcup _{i = 1, \ldots , n} X_{s_ i}$. Set $d = d_1\ldots d_ n$. It follows that $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}$ is globally generated by
L50: 
L51: \[ s_1^{d/d_1}, \ldots , s_ n^{d/d_ n}. \]
L52: This means that if $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes j}$ is globally generated then so is $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes j + dn}$ for all $n \geq 0$. Fix a $j \in \{ 0, \ldots , d - 1\} $. For any point $x \in X$ there exists an $n \geq 1$ and a global section $s$ of $\mathcal{L}^{j + dn}$ which does not vanish at $x$, as follows from (【15†5】) applied to $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{L}^{\otimes j}$ and ample invertible sheaf $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}$.
L53: Since $X$ is quasi-compact there we may find a finite list of integers $n_ i$ and global sections $s_ i$ of $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes j + dn_ i}$ which do not vanish at any point of $X$. Since $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}$ is globally generated this means that $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes j + dn}$ is globally generated where $n = \max \{ n_ i\} $.
L54: Since we proved this for every congruence class mod $d$ we conclude that there exists an $n_0 = n_0(\mathcal{L})$ such that $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}$ is globally generated for all $n \geq n_0$. At this point we see that if $\mathcal{F}$ is globally generated then so is $\mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}$ for all $n \geq n_0$.
L55: We continue to assume the equivalent conditions (1) – (6). Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_ X$-modules of finite type. Denote $\mathcal{F}_ n \subset \mathcal{F}$ the image of the canonical map of (【15†5】). By construction $\mathcal{F}_ n \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}$ is globally generated. By (【15†5】) we see $\mathcal{F}$ is the sum of the subsheaves $\mathcal{F}_ n$, $n \geq 1$.
L56: By Modules, Lemma 【30†17.9.7】 we see that $\mathcal{F} = \sum _{n = 1, \ldots , N} \mathcal{F}_ n$ for some $N \geq 1$. It follows that $\mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}$ is globally generated whenever $n \geq N + n_0(\mathcal{L})$ with $n_0(\mathcal{L})$ as above. We conclude that (1) – (6) implies (【31†7】).
L57: Assume (【31†7】). Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_ X$-modules of finite type. By (【31†7】) there exists an integer $n \geq 1$ such that the canonical map
L58: 
L59: \[ \Gamma (X, \mathcal{F} \otimes _{\mathcal{O}_ X} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}) \otimes _{\mathbf{Z}} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes -n} \longrightarrow \mathcal{F} \]
L60: is surjective. Let $I$ be the set of finite subsets of $\Gamma (X, \mathcal{F} \otimes _{\mathcal{O}_ X} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$ partially ordered by inclusion. Then $I$ is a directed partially ordered set. For $i = \{ s_1, \ldots , s_{r(i)}\} $ let $\mathcal{F}_ i \subset \mathcal{F}$ be the image of the map
L61: 
L62: \[ \bigoplus \nolimits _{j = 1, \ldots , r(i)} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes -n} \longrightarrow \mathcal{F} \]
L63: which is multiplication by $s_ j$ on the $j$th factor. The surjectivity above implies that $\mathcal{F} = \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}\nolimits _{i \in I} \mathcal{F}_ i$. Hence Modules, Lemma 【30†17.9.7】 applies and we conclude that $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F}_ i$ for some $i$. Hence we have proved (【16†8】). In other words, (【31†7】) $\Rightarrow $ (【16†8】).
L64: 
L65: The implication (【16†8】) $\Rightarrow $ (【32†9】) is trivial.
L66: Finally, assume (【32†9】). Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_ X$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. By Lemma 【33†28.23.3】 (this is where we use the condition that $X$ be quasi-separated) we see that $\mathcal{I} = \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}\nolimits _\alpha I_\alpha $ with each $I_\alpha $ quasi-coherent of finite type.
L67: Since by assumption each of the $I_\alpha $ is a quotient of negative tensor powers of $\mathcal{L}$ we conclude the same for $\mathcal{I}$ (but of course without the finiteness or boundedness of the powers). Hence we conclude that (【32†9】) implies (【26†6】). This ends the proof of the proposition. $\square$

L75: 【35†Comment #225】 by Ravi Vakil on June 07, 2013 at 18:05
